correctness.rationale: The frozen marginal, mean, composition table and crossing-edge refinement are numerically correct. I constructed the Fano graph from cyclic difference set {0,1,3}, traversed all 3432 labeled seven-subsets, and computed each binary rank from the size of the XOR span of the cut rows. Results include rank counts (100,980,1680,672) and exactly 336 rank-seven cuts at each of 11 and 13 crossing edges. The repaired contribution is the conditional edge profile, with a separate analytic proof. Character orthogonality yields a flat reduced spectrum of rank 2^r. Fano incidence rank four forces block sizes 3 and 4 for r=7; the four-block factors through the four augmented coordinates and is invertible exactly when the two complementary triples are bases. For any of the 28 point bases, 72 of the 168 ordered line bases pass det(N+J)≠0, by uniformity of N^−1 times the all-ones vector and its three even-weight values. Since both N and N+J are invertible, their row weights exclude total incidence counts other than 4 or 5, and complementation exchanges them. This leaves 6 unordered line bases per point basis per case; total cross edges are 3+2e. Hence there are 168 unordered cuts per edge count, or 336 oriented. At the all-edge cut the incidence rank is four. These checks support exactly the repaired finite theorem.
residual_risks: Exact ideal pure-state statement at this graph and balanced size; no noisy, weighted or larger-geometry extension.

value.rationale: The surviving result answers how many preparation edges can cross a balanced cut once maximal entanglement is imposed, for a canonical incidence graph. The complete two-class answer and short Fano-basis mechanism expose why the largest edge boundary need not be the best entanglement partition. It is a distinct and useful finite statistic, not a recomputation of the associated marginal histogram or a claim about practical gate cost.
residual_risks: No claim of extremal behavior in other states or noise/implementation benefit.
